ON FOOT

LMB: mine by hand, fire the rifle/lance, or grab/release with the tractor beam — whichever tool is selected

SHIFT+1-9,0 or click a slot picks a tool directly · Wheel: material (tractor: hold distance)
Tractor: SHIFT+mouse pitch/yaw · SHIFT+wheel roll · LMB on a drop collects it
[F] interact with what the reticle is ON — board a rocket, pick up or set down a log, pick up a stranded fish
Carry a felled log or stick bundle and turn hard to club attackers
Rope equipped + 2 in hand: [F] a carried log onto another log lashes them together
Oar equipped: [F] three rope-bound logs (side by side) to raft them — boards and paddles like the dugout canoe
Spear equipped: LMB throws it. No range limit — but it falls the whole way, so aim high for distance. Works under water (shorter, the water drags it). [F] to pick it back up where it lands

x-ray off
Draws the cave network through solid rock, sampled with the SAME predicate the cave mobs fly by. Cyan is natural cavern, amber is your own workings. Builds over ~2 s inside a frame budget rather than hitching.
UFO TRAFFIC --
Sends a real UFO out of a real hangar on the real route, forces the earth-like detour, and arms the dive. Nothing is teleported and nothing is shortened — the craft flies the whole crossing at cruise, circles the planet once, then goes down and leaves a wreck. Watch the readout below for the stage. Resets the once-per-system crash latch and clears any wreck already on the ground, so it can be run again.
--
Live, twice a second while this console is open. Nodes are that faction’s live installations — ground bases plus orbital stations; fewer than two and it has no route, so it will never launch anything, which is the routine case from system 2 on. Next roll is the soonest departure clock among its idle craft — a roll that can still be refused by the concurrency cap, or by the never-send-the-last-one-out rule. The crash latch is claimed once per system and never released, so an unspent latch is the only state in which a new crash can happen at all.

THIRD-PERSON CAMERA dead zone --
over the shoulder — shipped v2.11.57
The sight line lerps with pitch: high when looking level (view clears Bleaux’s head, and a trunk is struck well above the dirt) and low when looking down (so the aim can reach the near ground). Set both ends the same for a fixed-height rig. A hovering mech is always centred regardless of the lateral setting.
Dead zone is the nearest ground-resting hopper that can be brought under the crosshair at ANY pitch and yaw — measured live, by the same rule the camera flies by. A hopper attacks from about 2.0 u, so anything above that is a rig in which an attacking hopper cannot be shot. Lateral is signed: negative puts the camera over the LEFT shoulder. Third person only — [F4] switches. Not saved; a reload restores the shipped rig.

LOD & TERRAIN DETAIL clip --
Clip radius 0 = AUTO: the low-LOD shell is cut away out to the real chunk coverage minus the overlap, so valleys and water read at full detail. Sink and shell resolution re-bake the shell on release. Tier distances are in body radii and only affect bodies that are not chunk-streamed.

BLUE GORILLA

ASTRO MINING CO.

A Grey Alien family picnicked on a tropical mini-planet and left in a hurry — forgetting CHRiSPi, their egg-shaped CRISPR 3D printer, mid-print.

The print finished anyway. It was you: Bleaux, a blue gorilla with an upper-class accent and no idea where you are.

CHRiSPi wants to get home. Every planet and moon here hides a black hole bubble at its core. Mine minerals, print a rocket, harvest every bubble — and when the last one is taken, the sun itself will collapse into a black hole. Build a moscovium-hulled Starship and fly it into the black hole — that's the way to the next star system.
